Extra read-only folders you may use: handoff-docs, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fqq-Desktop-Topflightapps-roundai/2a408671-6ff1-4104-9d24-9f97da7d0ee6/scratchpad/cr/review-evidence

Scenario OAT-04/S19 — Every window is one configuration value (code and deployment review)

Requirements it checks:
- U12: All retention windows are configuration values, not hard-coded, so they can be lengthened later under a hospital affiliation.

Given: The main source at e02167f (read-only) and the local stack's environment only (never dev or production); one window of each class: 12 h, 16 h, 18 h, 36 h, Nursing Home visit count. The production environment check goes to Tim with S02
When: Find where each window in the TFA-94699 table is defined and how it would be lengthened
Then: Every window is read from one configuration value and no other code path has its own copy of the number; whether that value must be changeable without a code change and release is Q11
Oracle: UAT 3.6 / OAT-04 (B) 'all windows are configuration values, not hard-coded' and TFA-94699 AC 7. Both outcomes recorded now: the windows are named constants HOSPITAL_RETENTION / SNF_RETENTION in convex/lib/lifecycle.ts:8-38 with no env or settings row, so Pass if Q11 = 'a named constant is enough', Fail if Q11 = 'changeable without a release'. A second copy of a window number elsewhere in the code = Fail under either answer

THE ORACLE WINS. The question below only scopes this scenario to what code can decide. If the question, or its pass/fail rule, ever reads differently from the Then/Oracle above, follow the Then/Oracle, give the verdict the oracle gives, and say where they differ in openQuestions.

Open questions the oracle defers to, with the oracle's default for each (do not settle them yourself):
- pending:Q11 — oracle: "whether that value must be changeable without a code change and release is Q11". Default: named constants: Pass if Q11 = 'a named constant is enough', Fail if Q11 = 'changeable without a release'; a window defined only outside the config objects is labelled pending:Q11

Gaps the matrix already records (use the id in a label only when the finding is exactly that gap):
- known:K9 — the windows are module constants HOSPITAL_RETENTION / SNF_RETENTION with no env or settings row (matrix: "K9 (lifecycle.ts:8-38); verdict per Q11"); its verdict waits on Q11

YOUR QUESTION (answer this, from the code):
Find where each retention window of the TFA-94699 table (pre-round 12 h, Important Points 12 h, completed tasks 16 h, encounter / note 18 h, vitals-labs-imaging / meds / open tasks / handoffs 36 h, Nursing Home 2 visits) is defined and used across apps/web (convex and src). For every number you find outside HOSPITAL_RETENTION / SNF_RETENTION (convex/lib/lifecycle.ts), say which of two kinds it is: (a) a COPY: the config objects also define that window, and this code path holds its own number for it; (b) a window DEFINED ONLY OUTSIDE the config objects (they have no entry for it), e.g. a client-only label threshold.

pass = every window is defined once, in HOSPITAL_RETENTION / SNF_RETENTION, and read from there (no copy, nothing defined outside)
fail = (a) a second copy of a window number held elsewhere: a Fail under either answer to Q11 (label new); (b) a window defined only outside the config objects: Fail if Q11 = changeable without a release; under 'a named constant is enough' it depends on whether that window counts (label pending:Q11). The module constants themselves are known gap K9 (label known:K9)

Other halves of this scenario that another lane or a person runs (do not judge them; if the code you read predicts one of them, report that as a finding labelled half:<name>, supports = pass or fail):
- (none)

Not part of this verdict (other scenarios, or notes that decide nothing here):
- production environment check (Tim, with S02)



Label every finding:
- new: a failing point the matrix does not already record (supports = fail)
- known:<id>: exactly one of the recorded gaps listed above
- pending:<id>: a failing point whose verdict the oracle hands to one of the open questions above
- half:<name>: a point about one of the other halves above
- context: background, not for or against the verdict

Answer with: verdict (pass | fail | pending | unsure), answer (a short paragraph a QA lead can read: what the code does and why that is the verdict; name the recorded gaps and open questions it touches), findings (each with claim, file, line, quote, supports = pass | fail | context, label), physicianImpact, openQuestions, notDecidableByCode.
